name: Congenital Heart Defect-Ectodermal Dysplasia-Brachydactyly-Telangiectasia Syndrome
aliases: Congenital Heart Defect with Ectodermal Dysplasia and Brachydactyly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for CHDEBT Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of structural congenital heart defect confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac imaging
Clinical evidence of ectodermal dysplasia including abnormal hair, teeth, or sweat gland function
Radiologically confirmed shortening of the digits (brachydactyly)
Presence of cutaneous or mucosal telangiectasia
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital heart defect, ectodermal dysplasia features, and brachydactyly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Telangiectasia and family history support diagnosis but are not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ectodermal dysplasia with hypohidrosis and abnormal dentition
searchTerms: ectodermal problems with abnormal teeth and sweating

common.symptomName: Cutaneous telangiectasia on face and extremities
searchTerms: small red blood vessels on skin

common.symptomName: Dental anomalies including hypodontia and conical teeth
searchTerms: dental anomalies with small pointed teeth

common.symptomName: Exercise intolerance due to cardiac defect
searchTerms: tiredness with exercise due to heart problem
poor stamina related to cardiac issue
bleeding tendency in mouth and nose

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to cardiac defect
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from heart defect
pulmonary hypertension caused by heart problem
lung blood vessel pressure increased due to cardiac defect

laboratory: Reduced sweat chloride concentration indicating hypohidrosis
Mild anemia or thrombocytopenia in some cases
imaging: Echocardiography showing structural congenital heart defects (e.g., septal defects, valve anomalies)
genetic: Likely autosomal dominant inheritance pattern; specific gene not yet identified
other: Clinical examination revealing ectodermal dysplasia features and telangiectasia

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant vascular malformations without ectodermal dysplasia

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defect causing cyanosis or heart failure
Failure to thrive in infancy due to cardiac and ectodermal manifestations
